47:1: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Those who denied the Oneness of God and worshipped other than Him and turned away from those who wanted to worship Him and acknowledge His Oneness, and to believe in His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from what they wanted of Islam, acknowledgment, and belief, He has made their deeds misguided. He says: God made their deeds misguidance without guidance or righteousness, because they were done in the way of Satan and not on the right path.
47:2: And those who believed and did righteous deeds God Almighty says: And those who believed in God and acted in obedience to Him, and followed His commands and prohibitions and believed in what was revealed to Muhammad He says: And believed in the Book that God revealed to Muhammad and it is the truth from their Lord - He will remove from them their misdeeds He says: God erased from them because of their action the evil deeds they did, so He did not hold them accountable for it, nor did He punish them and set right their condition He says: And set right their affairs and their state in this world with His friends, and in the Hereafter by giving them inheritance of eternal bliss and everlasting immortality in His Paradise. It was mentioned that what he meant by his saying those who disbelieved...the verse were the people of Mecca, and those who believed and did righteous deeds...the verse were the people of Medina. Who said that? Ishaq bin Wahb Al-Wasiti told me: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya Al-Qattat, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, regarding his statement, Those who disbelieved and averted from the way of God, he said: It was revealed about the people of Mecca. And those who believed and did righteous deeds, he said: The Ansar. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of His saying, And He set right their condition, the people of interpretation said. Mention who told you: Ishaq bin Wahb Al-Wasiti told me: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya Al-Qattat, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas: And set their affairs right. He said: Their affairs. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And set their affairs right, he said: their condition. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And reform their condition. He said: He reformed their situation. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And set right their condition. He said: Their state. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And set right their condition, he said: Their state. And bal is like a verbal noun like shan from which no action is known, and the Arabs hardly ever pluralize it except in poetic necessity, and when they pluralize it they say balat.
47:3: God Almighty says: This is what We did to the two groups of misguiding the deeds of the disbelievers and atonement for those who believed and did righteous deeds, as a reward from Us to each group for their deeds. As for the disbelievers, We misguided their deeds and made them not on the right path and without guidance, because they followed Satan and obeyed him, which is falsehood. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida and Abbas bin Muhammad told me: Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us: Ibn Jurayj said: Khalid told me that he heard Mujahid say: That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood. He said: Falsehood is Satan. As for the believers, We have removed from them their misdeeds and amended their condition for them because they followed the truth that came to them from their Lord, which is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and what he brought to them from his Lord of light and proof. Thus does God set forth for the people their examples. God, the Almighty, says: Just as I have made clear to you, O people, so do the group of disbelievers and believers. Thus do We set forth examples for the people and make them resemble what is similar to them, so We ascribe to every people examples of similarities.
47:4: God Almighty says to the group of believers in Him and His Messengers: So when you meet those who disbelieve in God and His Messenger from among the people of war, strike their necks. And His statement, Until when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then secure their bonds, means: until when you have defeated them and subdued those of them whose neck you have not struck off, and they have become captives in your hands, then secure their bonds, meaning secure them in bonds so that they do not kill you and flee from you. And His statement, Either a favor from us afterwards or a ransom, means: If you take them captive after inflicting heavy casualties, then either you grant them a favor after that by releasing them from captivity and setting them free without compensation or ransom, or they ransom you by giving you from themselves in exchange until you release them and clear the way for them. Scholars differed regarding his statement, “Until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds. Then either accept a favor or ransom.” Some of them said: It is an abrogation of his statement, Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. (al-Tawbah 9:5) and his statement, But if you overtake them in battle, disperse by them those behind them. (al-Anfal 8:57). Who said that? Ibn Khameed and Ibn Isa Al-Damaghani told us: Al-Mubarak told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Jurayj that he used to say regarding His statement, Then either a favor from us afterwards or a ransom, it was abrogated by His statement, Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us on the authority of al-Suddi: Then either a favor from us afterwards or a ransom. He said: It was abrogated by Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. al-Tawbah 9:5 Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: He said: Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then either a favor from us afterwards or a ransom. This was abrogated by His statement: Then if you catch them in battle, disperse by them those behind them. al-Anfal 8:57 Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Sa`id told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, So when you meet those who disbelieve to His statement, or ransom, when the Muslims met the polytheists, they fought them. If they captured a prisoner among them, they had no choice but to ransom him or show him favor, then send him back. This was abrogated after His statement, But if you encounter them in war, disperse by them those behind them (al-Anfal 8:57). That is, admonish others besides them from among the people so that they might remember. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, who said: He wrote to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, about a prisoner, and he mentioned that they sought him for a ransom of such and such, so Abu Bakr said: Kill him for killing a polytheist, that is more beloved to me than such and such. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike [their] necks…to the end of the verse. He said: The ransom is abrogated. It was abrogated by: So when the sacred months have passed (al-Tawbah 9:5) to every place of ambush (al-Tawbah 9:5). He said: So there remained no covenant or sanctity for any of the polytheists after the disavowal and the passing of the sacred months. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Then either a favor from us afterward or a ransom, this is abrogated. It was abrogated by His statement, So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). So no covenant or protection remained for any of the polytheists after the disavowal. Others said: It is a decisive ruling and not abrogated. They said: It is not permissible to kill the prisoner, but it is permissible to grant him mercy and ransom him. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated: Abu Atab Sahl bin Hammad narrated: Khalid bin Jaafar narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein: Prisoners were brought to Al-Hajjaj, so he handed over a man to Ibn Umar to kill. Ibn Umar said: This is not our command. God the Almighty said: “Until, when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then secure their bonds. Then either a favor or a ransom.” He said: Weeping in front of him. Al-Hasan said: If this had happened, he and his companions would have rushed to them. Ibn Hamid and Ibn Isa Al-Damaghani told us: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, that he disliked killing a polytheist patiently. He said: And he would recite this verse: Then either a favor from us afterwards or a ransom. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: Do not kill prisoners except in war, to frighten the enemy. He said: Ibn Thaur narrated to us on the authority of Muammar, who said: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz would ransom them, one man for another, but Al-Hasan disliked ransoming them with money. He said: Ibn Thaur narrated to us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of a man from the people of Ash-Sham who was guarding Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and he was from Banu Asad, he said: I did not see Umar, may God have mercy on him, kill a prisoner except one from the Turks. Some Turkish prisoners were brought to him, and he ordered that they be enslaved. A man from among those who had brought them said: O Commander of the Faithful, if you had seen this one of them killing Muslims, you would have cried a lot over them. Umar said: Go ahead and kill him. So he went to him and killed him. And the correct statement in our view on this matter is that this verse is decisive and not abrogated. This is because the description of the abrogating and the abrogated is what we have explained in more than one place in our book, that is, unless the two of them are permissible to come together in one situation, or unless evidence has been established that one of them abrogates the other. It is not strange that the choice of favor, ransom, and killing was given to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to those who came after him in charge of the nation, even if the former was not mentioned in this verse, because he had permitted their killing in another verse, and that is His saying: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5)… The verse. Rather, it is like that, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to do this with those who became captives in his hand from the people of war, so he would kill some and ransom others, and show favor to others, like on the day of Badr, he killed Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt when he was brought as a captive, and he killed Banu Qurayzah when they submitted to the judgment of Sa’d, and they became in his hand peacefully, and he was able to ransom them and show favor to them, and he ransomed a group of captives. The polytheists who were taken captive at Badr, and Ali Thamama bin Aththal al-Hanafi, who was a prisoner in his hand, and this remained confirmed from his conduct among the people of war from the time God gave him permission to fight them, until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, always did that with them. Rather, God, may His praise be glorified, mentioned in this verse the favor and ransom for the captives, and He specifically mentioned them in it, because the command to kill them and His permission for that had been repeated in all the verses of His warning. So He informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what was mentioned in this verse of the favor and ransom, and what he had to do with them with the killing. And His statement, until the war lays down its burdens, means, “So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike their necks and do with their prisoners what I have made clear to you, until the war lays down its sins and the burdens of its people who associate others with God - they will not repent to God from their association with Him, and believe in Him and His messengers, and obey Him in His commands and prohibitions. That is the war laying down its burdens.” It was said, until the war lays down its burdens, meaning: until the war casts down the burdens of its people. It was said, the meaning of that is: until the warrior lays down his burdens. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us: Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, until war lays down its burdens, he said: Until Jesus, son of Mary, comes out, and every Jew, Christian, and follower of a religion will submit to Islam, and the sheep will be safe from the wolf, and no mouse will gnaw a hole in a bag, and enmity will disappear from all things. That will be the supremacy of Islam over all religions, and the Muslim man will be at ease until his foot drips with blood when he steps on it. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, until the war lays down its burdens, he said: until there is no more polytheism. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Until the war lays down its burdens. He said: Until there is no more polytheism. It was mentioned that he said: What is meant by war in this place is the warriors. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: Until the war lays down its burdens. He said: War: whoever was fighting them called them war. And His statement, “That is so. And if God had willed, He could have taken revenge on them.” God Almighty says: This that I have commanded you to do, O believers, of killing the polytheists when you encounter them in war, and binding them up after subduing them, and taking them captive, and offering them favors and ransoms until the war lays down its burdens. This is the truth that your Lord has imposed upon you. And if your Lord had willed, He could have taken revenge on these polytheists about whom He has made this ruling clear, with a punishment from Him for them immediately, and that would have sufficed you with all of that. But God Almighty disliked taking revenge on them and punishing them immediately except by your hands, O believers. That He may test you by means of others. He says: That He may test you by means of them, so that He may know the mujahidin among you and the patient ones, and He may test them by means of you, so that He may punish by means of your hands whomever He wills of them, and take heed from whomever He wills of them by means of those who destroyed by means of your hands whomever He wills of them until they turn to the truth. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And if God had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them. Yes, by God, with His many armies, all of His creation is an army, and if He had given power to the weakest of His creation, they would be an army. And His statement, And those who fought in the way of God: The reciters differed in the recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Kufa recited and those who fought meaning: they fought the polytheists and struggled against them, with an alif. Al-Hasan Al-Basri, as reported from him, used to recite it they killed with a damma on the qaf and a shaddah on the ta’, meaning: the polytheists killed them one after the other, but he did not name the doers. It was reported from Jahdary Asim that he used to recite it they killed with a fatha on the qaf and a soft ta’, meaning: and those who killed the polytheists for the sake of God. Abu Amr used to recite it they killed with a damma on the qaf and a soft ta’, meaning: and those who killed the polytheists. Then he omitted the doers, making them so that the doer of that was not named for them. The most correct reading is the reading of man qaraman qarahu and those who fought due to the agreement of the argument of the reciters, even though all of them have understandable aspects. And since this is the most correct reading for us, the interpretation of the statement is: And those who fought among you, O believers, against the enemies of God from among the disbelievers in the religion of God, and in support of the guidance that He sent His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with, so strive against them in that, He will not let their deeds go astray. So God will not make the deeds that they did in this world a misguidance for them, just as He let the deeds of the disbelievers go astray. It was mentioned that this verse refers to the people of Uhud. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And those who are killed in the way of God - He will never let their deeds perish. It was mentioned to us that this verse was revealed on the Day of Uhud, while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in the valley, and wounds and killing had spread among them. The polytheists had cried out: “One day for another. War is a contest. We have a support for you.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God is our protector, and you have no protector. The dead will be varied. As for those who are killed, they are alive and provided for, but as for your dead, they will be tormented in the Fire.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And those who are killed in the way of God - never will He let their deeds perish. He said: Those who were killed on the day of Uhud.
47:5: God Almighty says: God Almighty will guide those who fought in His cause to work in a way that pleases Him and will set right their condition in this world and the next. And admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them. He says: And God will admit them to His Paradise, which He has made known to them. He says: He has made it known and made it clear to them, so that a man will come to his home in it when he enters it just as he came to his home in this world, and that will not be difficult for him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: When God saves the believers from the Fire, they will be detained on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and some of them will take revenge on others for the many injustices that occurred between them in this world. Then they will be given permission to enter Paradise. He said: The believer will not be more certain of his status in Paradise when he enters it. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them, he said: meaning their dwellings therein. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them, he said: Its people will be guided to their homes and dwellings, and where God has allotted them, they will not make mistakes, as if they had been its inhabitants since their creation, not asking anyone to guide them to it. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Yazid said regarding His statement, And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them, he said: It has reached us from more than one person who said: The people of Paradise will enter Paradise, and they will know their dwellings in it better than their dwellings in this world, which they will go to in the course of their life in this world. He said: So that is the statement of God, the Most High, And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them.
47:6: God Almighty says: And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them.
47:7: And His statement, O you who have believed, if you support God, He will support you. God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, if you support God, He will support you by your support of them and grant you victory over them, for He is the supporter of His religion and His allies. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, If you support God, He will support you, because it is God’s right to give to whoever asks Him, and to support whoever supports Him. His saying, And makes your feet firm, means: He strengthens you against them and makes you bold, so that you do not turn away from them, even if their number is great and your number is small.
47:8: God Almighty says: And those who disbelieved in God and denied His Oneness, so woe to them meaning: shame, misery, and affliction for them. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Those who disbelieve - then woe to them, he said: Misery to them. His statement, And He has made their deeds worthless, means that He made their deeds done without guidance or righteousness, because they were done in obedience to Satan, not in obedience to the Most Merciful. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of those who said that: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And He rendered their deeds worthless, that he said: The misguidance that God led them astray is that He did not guide them as He guided others. The misguidance that God told you about is: He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills. He said: These are among those whose deeds He made misguidance. His statement, And He rendered their deeds worthless, was responded to His statement, He wills, “So woe to them,” which is a past tense verb, and woe is a noun because even though woe is a noun, it has the meaning of a verb because of the meaning of a supplication in it. So it means: May God make them wretched, and for that reason He returned He rendered them worthless, because a supplication is like a command and a prohibition. Similarly, His statement, Until, when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then tighten the bonds, was responded to an implied command that makes striking worse.
47:9: And His statement, That is because they hated what God revealed, God Almighty says: This that We did to them of misery and misguidance of deeds is because they hated Our Book that We revealed to Our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and were displeased with it, so they denied it and said: It is obvious magic. His statement, So He rendered their deeds worthless, means: He rendered worthless the deeds they did in this world, namely their worship of deities. God did not benefit them by them in this world or in the Hereafter, but rather He destroyed them by them, and cast them into a Blaze. This is the judgment of God, the Majestic and Glorious, on all those nations who disbelieved in Him, as Qatada said. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, So woe to them, he said: It is general for the unbelievers.
47:10: God the Almighty says: Did not these disbelievers travel through the land to see Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and what was revealed to him of the Book? This is only a rebuke from God to them, because they used to travel to Syria, to see the punishment of God that He brought upon the people of Hijr and Thamud, and they saw in their travel to Yemen what God brought upon Sheba. So He said to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and to the believers in him: Did not these polytheists travel through the land to see what was the end of the denial of those before them from the nations who denied their messengers and rejected their advice? Did We not destroy them, demolishing their homes and laying them in ruins? So they would learn a lesson from that and beware that God would do that to them for their denial of him, so they would return to obeying God and believing in you? Then He, the Most High, threatened them and informed them that if they persisted in their denial of His Messenger, He would bring upon them a punishment similar to that which He brought upon the nations before them. He said: And for the disbelievers is the like of it. He said: And for the disbelievers from Quraysh who denied the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there is an immediate punishment similar to the consequence of the nations who came before them denying their messengers because of their denial of His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Rawqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And for the disbelievers is the like of it, he said: The like of what the first generations were destroyed by, a warning from God to them.
47:11: God Almighty says: This action that we did to these two groups: the group of disbelief, from our victory over the group of faith in God and our making their feet firm, and our destruction of the group of disbelief because God is the protector of those who believe meaning: because God is the protector of those who believe in Him and obey His Messenger. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ both on the authority of Abu Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, That is because God is the protector of those who believe, he said: Their protector. It was mentioned to us that this is in Abdullah’s reading, that God is the protector of those who believe, and that which is in the table, which is in our copies of the Qur’an, Your protector is only God and His Messenger (al-Ma’idah 5:5), your protector is only God, in his reading. And His saying: And that the disbelievers have no protector, means: And that the disbelievers in God have no protector or helper.
47:12: And His statement, Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. God Almighty says: Indeed, God has the divinity that belongs to no one else. He will admit those who believe and His Messenger to gardens beneath whose trees rivers flow. He does this to them as an honor for their belief in Him and in His Messenger. And His statement, And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as livestock eat, meaning, “And those who denied the Oneness of God and denied His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, enjoy themselves in this world with its debris, its feathers, and its vanishing, fading adornments, and they eat in it without thinking about the Hereafter, and without considering what God has placed for His creation of proofs leading them to the knowledge of the Oneness of God and the truthfulness of His Messengers. So their example in eating what they eat in it without their knowledge of that, and without understanding, is like that of livestock from the beasts that are subjugated and whose only concern is feeding and nothing else. “And the Fire will be their abode,” meaning, And the Fire is the fire of Hell, meaning, and the Fire is their dwelling place and a refuge to which they will go after their death.
47:13: God Almighty says: How many, O Muhammad, are there towns stronger than your town? He says: Its people were stronger in strength, more numerous, and more numerous than the people of your town, which is Mecca. He excluded the report from the town, but what is meant by it are its people. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And how many a town was stronger than your town which expelled you, but We destroyed them? He said: It is Mecca. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And how many a city was mightier than your city, he said: His city was Mecca. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Al-Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hubaysh, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that when the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left Mecca to fight, I think he said: To Mecca. He said: You are the most beloved of God's lands to God, and you are the most beloved of God's lands to me. If the polytheists had not expelled me, I would not have left you. The most stubborn of enemies were those who transgressed against God by violating the sanctity of God, or killed someone other than his killer, or killed with the filth of the Age of Ignorance. So God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: And how many a city was mightier in power than your city which expelled you? We destroyed them, and none could help them. And God, the Most High, said: I expelled you. He made the report about the city, and that is why He made it feminine. Then He said: We destroyed them, because the meaning of His statement: I expelled you is what I described, that it is intended for the people of the city. So He made the report sometimes according to the wording, and sometimes according to the meaning. His statement, So they have no helper has two interpretations: One of them is that its meaning, even if the helper was made accusative by exoneration, is: So they have no helper, and that is because the Arabs sometimes omit the word was in such a situation. The other is that its meaning is: So they have no helper now from the punishment of God to aid them.
47:14: God Almighty says: “Is he who is on proof, evidence, and explanation of the command of his Lord and knowledge of His Oneness, so he worships Him with insight from Him, that he has a Lord who will reward him for his obedience to Him with Paradise, and for his evil and disobedience to Him with Hellfire, like one to whom Satan has made his evil deeds seem attractive, so he sees them as beautiful, so he persists in doing them, and they follow their desires,” meaning: and they follow what their souls have called them to of disobeying God and worshipping idols, without having any proof or evidence for what they do of that? It was said that the one meant by His statement: Is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord is our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the one meant by His statement: like he who has made his evil deeds seem attractive are the polytheists.
47:15: His mention says: The description of Paradise that I have promised to the righteous, and they are those who feared His punishment in this world, the luxurious obligations, and avoided His sins In it are rivers of water that is not stagnant. His mention says: In Paradise that he mentioned that it is from this, other than its fragrance, he admitted from it: This delight has become stagnant, the water of the well: If the fragrance of what you hear changes, then it is stagnant, and likewise for the man if a foul odor is invented: It has become stagnant, so it is stagnant. As for if the water becomes stagnant and changes, then it is possible that it has: It has become stagnant, so it is stagnant, and stagnant water. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of from water that is not stagnant, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us: Ali told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Therein are rivers of water that is not stagnant, he said: Not varied. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding that it is from water that is not stagnant, he said: from water that is not putrid. Isa bin Amr told me: Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us: Mus`ab bin Salam told us, on the authority of Sa`d bin Tarif: Abu Ishaq’s question about non-stagnant water: I asked Al-Harith about it, and he told me that the non-stagnant water is Tasnim. He said: I have been informed that no hand touches it, the water comes like this until it enters his mouth. He said, And rivers of fine milk. He said, “Its mention is that it is from the milk of a camel, not from the udder, because it was not permissible for the animal to change its taste by exiting the udders, but God created it from the beginning in the rivers, so it is in a good form because it is built upon it.” He says: And rivers of wine, a delight for the drinkers. He says: And in it are rivers of wine, a delight for the drinkers, who take pleasure in drinking it. As Issa told me, he said: Ibn Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, he said: Mus`ab Sa`d bin Tarif told us, he said: I asked Al-Harith about it, and he said: The Magi did not step on it, nor did Satan blow into it, nor did the sun harm it, but it is fragrant. He said: I said to Karma: What is fragrant? He said: Glutin. Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: Hafs bin Omar told us: Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: From milk whose taste I have not tasted. He said: It has not been milked. And the word lust is in the genitive case as a description of wine, and it is decided to raise it as a description of rivers, which is permissible, or it is in the accusative case as in to enjoy it with pleasure, as was mentioned later: This is a gift to you, which was permissible. As for the reading, I do not permit it except in the genitive case due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. And he says, Rivers of purified honey, meaning: It is from honey that has been purified from impurities, and what is in the honey of the people of this world before the Creator, He informed His servants of His mention, and this prophet said that purified means that it was created in rivers initially from running water, the water and the honey are easy in it, so for that reason it is purified, God purified it from the impurities that are in the honey of the people of this world, which does not become pure from impurities except after filtration, because it was in wax and was purified from it. And He says to him, And for them therein are all kinds of fruits. He says, And for these righteous people in this Paradise are from these rivers that we mentioned, from all the fruits that are formed from deeds. “And forgiveness from their Lord.” He says, And forgiveness from God for their sins in this world, then they repented from them, and their Lord pardoned them. And he says, Like one who is eternally in the Fire. He says, He who is safe in this Paradise, which we have described, is like one who is eternally in the Fire. And the speech began with a description of Paradise, so it was said: Like Paradise which was promised to the righteous, and it was not said: He who is safe is in Paradise, then a sentence after the judgment of the report about Paradise, its description, Like one who is eternally in the Fire. The formation of that is like that, sufficing with the listener’s knowledge of the speech, and to indicate that he said, Like one who is eternally in the Fire, on the meaning of Like Paradise which the righteous were promised. He says, And His strength is available. He says, And He gave to drink the fire those who are eternal in the water, and the freedom of that water has ended with them. Muhammad Khalaf al-Asqalani told me: Haywa bin Shureih al-Himsi told us: Baqiyah told us on the authority of Safwan bin Amr: Ubayd God bin Bishr told us on the authority of Imam Umamah al-Bahili on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he choked: And he is given to drink from a water of purulent blood, gulping it down: 16 He said: What is close to him and he dislikes it, he touches something close to him, he is slightly directed towards it, and the blow falls immediately, three times he drinks, his intestines are cut off until it comes out of his anus, he said: And only good legs on their intestines God Almighty says: He complains of an evil drink and an evil resting place Al-Kahf.
47:16: His mention says: And among these infidels, O Muhammad, is he who listens to you and he is the hypocrite, in listening to what you say but does not comprehend or understand it, out of negligence of what you recite to him from the Book of your Lord, and neglecting what you say and call to of faith until when they go out from you they said, informing those who attended your meeting from the people of knowledge of the Book of God, and their recitation of what you recited, and it was said to them what you said that they will not listen attentively to your words and recitation What did Muhammad say to us just now? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Aqtada: And among them are those who listen to you until, when they leave you, these are the hypocrites. A man entered: a man who understood from God and benefited from what he heard, and a man who did not understand from God and did not benefit from what he heard. He was held back. People are three types: a listener who acts, a listener who is heedless, and a listener who betrays. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And among them are those who enjoy themselves with you. He said: They are the hypocrites. And concealing: The three types of al-Nas 114:one who listens and acts, one who listens and is heedless, and one who listens and then abandons. Abu Kuraib told us: Yahya bin Adam told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Yaqzan, on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazza or Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: I am one of them, and I was asked among those who were asked. Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about eating: And among them are those who enjoy themselves with you until, when they leave you... and the end of the verse, he said: These are the hypocrites, and those who were given knowledge: the Companions, may God be pleased with them. And He says, Those are the ones upon whom God has sealed, His mention says: These are the ones whose description is the nationalists upon whose hearts God has sealed, so they are not guided to the truth with which God sent His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and follow their desires, meaning: They rejected God’s command and followed what came to them, so they do not return from what their hearts are upon to the truth or proof. And He, the Most High, then made a distinction between the description of the hypocrites and the polytheists, in that all of them follow their desires in what they are upon from their separation from the religion of God with which He sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So He said about these hypocrites, The fruits of those upon whose hearts God has sealed and who follow their desires, and He said about the people of disbelief in Him from the people of polytheism, Like one to whom his evil deed has been made attractive and who follows their desires. al-Tawbah 9:37
47:17: God the Most High says: As for those whom God has guided to follow the truth and opened their hearts to believe in Him and in His Messenger, from among those who listened to you, O Muhammad, then what you recited to them and what they heard from you, He increased them in guidance. He says: God increased their faith in the truth of what you brought to them from God, in addition to the explanation they had. It was mentioned that what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to them from the Qur’an, the hypocrites among them said to the people of faith: What did he say just now? God increased the guidance of the people of guidance among them. Some of what God revealed from the Qur’an abrogates some of what had been previously ruled. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness, he said: When God revealed the Qur’an, they believed in it, so it was guidance. Then, when the abrogating and abrogated verses became clear, He increased them in guidance. And His statement, And He gave them their piety, God Almighty says: And God gave these guided ones their piety, and that is because He used them to piety towards Him.

ََْوََُْْ ُْصاَح ًََن قَاْة اََاََن معم،ثَا اَن ثور: ْاََلى قاَََْنْحْثَا محم. ًََُْن ََوَوا َو ََوَوا َِا َْمَََُْى: ْقاََُْْ ََُِْا قاَُْفاَى َََُْْفي فاَى َِاَْاَن ز: ْقا: َْخَََا اَن وُب قا:
