47:19: 19 - Know that there is no god but God meaning, O Muhammad, for your knowledge of that which is beneficial on the Day of Resurrection and seek forgiveness for your sin for which he was told that along with his infallibility so that his nation would follow his example, and he did so. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I seek forgiveness from God a hundred times every day and for the believing men and believing women in this is an honor for them by commanding their Prophet to seek forgiveness for them and God knows your movements your actions in your daytime occupations and your resting place your place of rest when you go to bed at night, meaning He knows all of your conditions, nothing of them is hidden from Him, so beware of Him. The address is to the believers and others. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Know, O Muhammad, that there is no deity worthy of being worshipped or fit to be worshipped, and that it is permissible for you and creation to worship Him, except God, who is the Creator of creation and the Owner of all things. Everything below Him owes Him Lordship. And ask forgiveness for your sin and ask your Lord for forgiveness for your past and future sins - and the sins of the men and women who believe in you. And God knows your movements and your resting places meaning: God knows your actions in what you do when you are awake, and your resting places when you go to sleep at night. Nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for all of that. Abu Kuraib narrated to us: Uthman bin Saeed narrated to us: Ibrahim bin Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abdullah bin Sarjis, who said: “I ate with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: ‘May God forgive you, O Messenger of God.’ A man from among the people said: ‘Shall I seek forgiveness for you, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘Yes, for you.’ Then he recited: ‘And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women.’”
47:20: God the Almighty says: And those who believe in God and His Messenger say, Why was a surah not revealed from God commanding us to wage jihad against the enemies of God from among the disbelievers? “But when a decisive surah is revealed,” meaning: one that is decisive in explanation and obligations. He mentioned that in that is the recitation of Abdullah, But when a newly invented surah is revealed. His saying, And he mentioned fighting therein, means: And he mentioned fighting the polytheists therein. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told me: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And those who believe say, ‘Why was a surah not sent down?’ But when a clear surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned therein, he said: Every surah in which jihad is mentioned is clear, and it is the most severe of the Qur’an against the hypocrites. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And fighting is mentioned in it. He said: Every surah in which fighting is mentioned is decisive. And His statement, I saw those in whose hearts is disease, means: I saw those in whose hearts is doubt and weakness in the religion of God, looking at you, O Muhammad, with the look of one fainting from death, fearing that you might attack them and command them to fight with the Muslims. So out of fear of that and to avoid meeting the enemy, they look at you with the look of one fainting from a fall. And what He meant by His statement, from death, is the fear of death, and this was the action of the hypocrites. Like what Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, They look at you with the look of one fainting from death, he said: These are the hypocrites whose hearts God has sealed, so they do not understand what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is saying. And His saying, It is more fitting for them, God Almighty says: It is more fitting for those in whose hearts is disease. His saying, It is more appropriate for them is a warning with which God has threatened these hypocrites. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, It is more appropriate for them, he said: This is a threat, so it is more appropriate for them, then the speech was cut off and he said, Obedience and good speech. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, It is more appropriate for them, he said: A threat as you hear.
47:21: And His saying, Obedience and appropriate speech. This is report from God, the Most High, about what these hypocrites said before a decisive surah was revealed, in which fighting was mentioned, and that if it was said to them, God has made jihad obligatory upon you, they would say, I hear and obey. So God, the Most High, said to them, When a surah is revealed, and fighting is made obligatory upon them, and this is difficult for them, and they dislike it, Obedience and appropriate speech, before the obligation is made obligatory upon you, so when the matter is decided, you dislike it and it is difficult for you. His saying, Obedience and good speech is raised by an implied subject, which is your saying before the revelation of the obligation of fighting, Obedience and good speech. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas with an unsatisfied chain of transmission that he said: God Almighty said, So it is more appropriate for them, then He said to those who believed among them, Obedience and appropriate speech. This statement completes the threat, so it is more appropriate. Then it is resumed after, and it is said, Obedience and appropriate speech, so obedience is lifted by His statement to them. Mujahid used to say about this: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Obedience and good speech. He said: God commanded the hypocrites to do that. His saying, Then when the matter is decided, means: When fighting becomes obligatory and God’s command comes, you will hate it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us. Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And when the matter is decided, he said: When the matter becomes serious. This is what Muhammad ibn Amr said in his hadith, on the authority of Abu Asim. Al-Harith said in his hadith, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The matter becomes serious. And His statement, If they had been true to God, it would have been better for them, God Almighty says: If they had been true to God in what they promised Him before the revelation of the Surah about fighting, by saying when it was said to them, God will command you to fight in obedience, and they obeyed Him in that, it would have been better for them in their immediate worldly life and in their later life. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: So when the matter is decided, he says: Obedience to God and His Messenger, and good speech when the facts of matters are known is better for them. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada, who said: Obedience to God and speaking what is right when matters are true is better for them.
47:22: God Almighty says to those who, when a decisive surah was revealed and fighting was mentioned in it, looked at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the look of one who has fainted, Then will you not O people, meaning: Perhaps if you turn away from the revelation of God, may He be glorified, and abandon the rulings of His Book, and turn away from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought to you, that you will cause corruption on earth meaning: that you will disobey God on earth, disbelieve in Him, and shed blood therein, and sever your ties of kinship and return to what you were upon in your ignorance of dispersion and division after God has united you in Islam and united your hearts through it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Then would you, if you were to turn away?...the verse. He says: Would you then see how the people were when they turned away from the Book of God? Did they not shed unlawful blood, sever family ties, and disobey the Most Merciful? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: Would you then, if you were given authority, cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship? He said: They did. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and Sulayman ibn Bilal told us: Mu`awiyah ibn Abi al-Mazard al-Majini told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “God created the creation, and when He finished with them, the womb clung to the right of the Most Merciful. He said: ‘Stop!’ It said: ‘This is the station of one who seeks refuge in You from being severed.’ He said: ‘Would you not be pleased that I sever ties with him who severed ties with you, and connect ties with him who connected ties with you?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Then that is for you.’” Sulayman said in his hadith: Abu Hurayrah said: Read if you wish: So would you, if you were given authority, cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship? Some of them interpreted it as: So would you, if you were given authority over the affairs of the people, cause corruption in the land in the sense of authority? The reciters other than Nafi’ agreed to open the seen in ‘asitum, while Nafi’ used to break it in ‘asitum. The correct view in our opinion is to say that with the fat-ha on the seen, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, and that it has not been heard in speech: ‘Asaa Akhuka Yaqum, with the kasra on the seen and the fat-ha on the ya. If it had been correct to break it if a noun is connected to it, it would have been broken with the non-makun. In their consensus on opening it with the apparent noun, there is clear evidence that it is the same with the makun. And that which follows ‘Asyatum is broken, and it is a letter of recompense, and that which is with Tafsadou is in the accusative position with ‘Asyatum.
47:23: And His statement, Those are the ones whom God has cursed, God Almighty says: These are the ones who do this, meaning those who corrupt and sever family ties, whom God has cursed and distanced from His mercy and made deaf, meaning: He has stripped them of their understanding of what they hear with their ears of God’s admonitions in His revelation. And He has blinded their sight, meaning: He has stripped them of their minds, so they do not discern God’s proofs, nor do they remember what they see of His lessons and evidence.
47:24: God Almighty says: Do these hypocrites not ponder the admonitions of God in the verses of the Qur’an that He revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and reflect on His arguments that He made clear to them in His revelation so that they may know from them the error of what they are adhering to? Or are there locks upon their hearts? He says: Or has God locked their hearts so that they do not understand what God has revealed in His Book of admonitions and lessons. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Do they not then reflect upon the Qur’an, or are there locks upon their hearts? Then, by God, they find in the Qur’an a deterrent against disobeying God, if only the people had reflected upon it and understood it. But they took to the ambiguous, and so they perished in that. Ismail bin Hafs Al-Ayli narrated to us, he said: Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Thawr bin Yazid, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, he said: There is no human being but that he has four eYa-Sin 36:two eyes in his head for his worldly life and what will benefit him in his livelihood, and two eyes in his heart for his religion and what God has promised of the unseen. So if God intends good for a servant, the two eyes in his heart see, and if God intends something else for him, He blinds them. This is what He said: Or are there locks upon their hearts? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Thawr bin Yazid told us: Khalid bin Ma’dan told us: There is no one among the people who does not have four eyes, two eyes in his face for his livelihood, and two eyes in his heart. There is no one who does not have a devil lurking in the back of his spine, bending his neck over his neck, opening his mouth to the fruit of his heart. So if God wants good for a servant, his two eyes in his heart see what God has promised of the unseen, so he acts upon it, and they are unseen, so he acts upon the unseen. But if God wants evil for a servant, He leaves him. Then he recited: Or are there locks upon the hearts? Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Thawr, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, in a similar manner, except that he said: Leaving the heart as it is. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us: Hammad bin Zaid told us: Hisham bin Urwah told us on the authority of his father who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited one day: ‘Do they not then reflect upon the Qur’an, or are there locks upon their hearts?’ A young man from Yemen said: ‘Rather, they have locks upon them until God, the Almighty, removes them.’ So the young man remained in the heart of Umar, may God be pleased with him, until he assumed power and sought his help.”
47:25: And His statement, Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them God Almighty says, “Indeed, those who turned back on their heels, disbelieving in God after the truth had become clear to them and they had established the right path, and they knew the clear proof, then they preferred misguidance over guidance, out of obstinacy to the command of God Almighty after they had knowledge.” Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, those who turned back after guidance had become clear to them are the enemies of God, the People of the Book. They know that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were sent to them, but then they disbelieve in him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada, After guidance has become clear to them, that they find it written down with them. Others said: He meant the hypocrites. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Indeed, those who turned back upon their heels... to His statement, and rendered worthless their deeds, they are the people of hypocrisy. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, those who turn back on their heels…to their secrets, they are the hypocrites. This description of the hypocrites in our view is more similar to the description of the People of the Book than it is to the description of the People of the Book. This is because God, the Exalted, the Majestic, has informed us that their apostasy was because they said, For those who hate what God has revealed, We will obey you in some of the matter. If it were to be described as the People of the Book, then describing them as having denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have been sufficient to inform us that they only apostatized because of what they said. And His statement, Satan enticed them, means that God Almighty says: Satan made their apostasy attractive to them, after guidance had become clear to them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: Satan tempted them and gave them hope. He said: He made things seem good to them. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Make it seem good to them. His saying, And He granted them respite, means: God extended their life span for them for a period of time. The meaning of the statement is: Satan tempted them, and God granted them respite. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Kufa recited it as wa amlā lihum with a fathah on the alif, meaning: and God dictated to them. Some of the people of Medina and Basra recited it as wa amlā lihum without naming the agent. Mujahid read, as mentioned by him, and dictated, with the alif closed and the ya’ extended, as a statement from God, may He be glorified and praised, about Himself that He will do that for them. The first of these readings to be correct, which is the one followed by the majority of the readers of Hijaz and Kufa, is the opening of the alif in that, because it is the widespread reading in the readings of the regions, even if they are united by a doctrine in which their meanings are similar.
47:26: God Almighty says: God granted these hypocrites respite and left them, and Satan tempted them, so He did not guide them to guidance because they said to those who hated what God had revealed of the command to fight the polytheists who associated partners with Him: We will obey you in some of the matter, which is contrary to the command of God Almighty and the command of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: That is because they said to those who hated what God revealed, ‘We will obey you in some of the matter.’ These are the hypocrites. And God knows their secrets. God Almighty says: And God knows the secrets of these two parties who are demonstrating from among the hypocrites, in opposition to the command of God and the command of His Messenger, as they whisper among themselves about disbelief in God and disobeying the Messenger, and neither that nor any other matter is hidden from Him. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as asrarhum with a fatha on the alif from asrarhum as a plural of sirra. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as israrhum with a kasra on the alif as a verbal noun from asrartu isrartu. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.
47:27: God Almighty says: And God knows the secrets of these hypocrites, so how could He not know their state when the angels take their souls while they are striking their faces and backs? He says: Their state at that time will not be hidden from Him either. And by turning away He means: the miracle, and we have already mentioned the narration about that previously.
47:28: And His statement, That is because they followed that which angered God, God Almighty says: The angels do this to the hypocrites that I described them with because they followed that which angered God, so He became angry with them by obeying Satan. And they hated His pleasure, He says: And they hated what would please Him with them by fighting the infidels with it, after He had made it obligatory upon them. His saying, So He rendered their deeds worthless, means: So God rendered their deeds worthless and made them go away, because they were done without His pleasure or love, so they became worthless and did not benefit the one who did them.
47:29: God the Almighty says: Do these hypocrites who have doubts in their hearts about their religion, and weakness in their certainty, and are confused about knowing the truth, think that God will not bring forth in their hearts the grudges against the believers, and change them for them and reveal them, until they know their hypocrisy and their confusion about their religion? And if We willed, We could show you them God the Almighty says: And if We willed, O Muhammad, We could make these hypocrites known to you so that you would know them, from the saying of the one who says: I will show you what I do, meaning I will teach you. And His statement, Then you will recognize them by their mark, means: You will recognize them by the signs of hypocrisy that are apparent in their words and actions. Then God, the Most High, made them known to you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Or do those in whose hearts is disease think that God will not bring to light their hatred…to the end of the verse, he said: They are the people of hypocrisy, and He defined them in Bara’ah and said: And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave and He said: Then say, You will never enter into conflict with me, nor will you fight with me an enemy. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Or do those in whose hearts is disease think that God will not bring to light their hatred,… the verse, that they are the people of hypocrisy, You would know them by their mark, and you will surely know them by the tone of their speech. So God made them known to him in Surat At-Tawbah, and He said, And never pray over any of them who dies, and He said, Then say to them, ‘You will never go forth with me, nor will you fight with me an enemy.’ Yunus told me, who said: Ibn Wahb told us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Or do those in whose hearts is disease think that God will not bring to light their hatred, that they are the hypocrites. He said: What they concealed of hypocrisy is disbelief.
47:30: He said: Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And if We willed, We could have shown them to you, and you would have known them by their mark, that they were the hypocrites. He said: And God showed them to him, and ordered them to leave the mosque. He said: But they refused except to hold fast to There is no god but God. So when they refused except to hold fast to There is no god but God, their blood was spared, and they married and were married to because of it. And his saying, And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech, means: And you will surely recognize these hypocrites by the meaning of their speech, something similar. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, In the melody of speech, that their statement, And God knows your deeds, does not conceal from Him the one among you who acts in obedience to Him, nor the one who disobeys that, and He will reward all of you for it.
47:31: God Almighty says to the people of faith from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, And We will surely test you, O believers, with killing and jihad against the enemies of God, “until We make evident those among you who strive in jihad for God’s sake, and those who are patient in fighting His enemies, so that this becomes clear to you, and those among you who have insight into His religion are known from those who have doubts and confusion about it, and the people of faith from the hypocrites, and We will test your report and We will make evident those among you who are truthful from those who are lying. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “Until We know those who strive among you and the patient,” and His statement, And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger, and something similar to this. He said: God Almighty informed the believers that this world is a house of trial, and that He will test them in it, and He commanded them to be patient, and gave them good tidings, saying, And give good tidings to the patient, then He informed them that this is what He did with His prophets and chosen ones so that their souls would be at ease, and He said, Poverty and hardship have touched them, and they have been shaken, poverty is poverty, and hardship is illness, and they have been shaken by trials and the harm people cause them. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And We will surely test you until We make evident those among you who strive [for the cause of God] and the steadfast, He said: We will test you. Testing means trial. And he recited, “Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left to say, ‘We believe’ and they will not be tested?” He said: They will not be tested. And We have certainly tested those before them...the verse. The reciters differed regarding the statement, And We will surely test you until We make evident those who strive among you and the patient and We will make evident your report. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it with the letter nun as nabulu and ya’lam and nablau as a statement from God, the Majestic and Sublime, about Himself, except for Asim who read it with the letter ya and the letter nun. The first reading is the reading according to us due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, even though the other reading has a correct interpretation.
47:32: And His statement, Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted from the way of God means, the Most High said: Indeed, those who denied the Oneness of God and averted people from the religion with which He sent His Messengers, and opposed the Messenger after guidance had become clear to them means: and they opposed His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they fought him and harmed him after they knew that he was a prophet sent and a messenger sent, and they knew the clear path by knowing him, and that he is a Messenger of God. His statement, They will not harm God at all, is because God will accomplish His purpose and support His Messenger and make him prevail over those who oppose and oppose Him. And He will render their deeds worthless, meaning: He will make the deeds they did in this world go away, so they will not benefit them in this world or the Hereafter, and He will nullify them from what harms them.
47:33: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, obey God and obey the Messenger in their commands and prohibitions, and do not invalidate your deeds. He says: Do not invalidate the reward for your deeds by disobeying them and disbelieving in your Lord, because disbelief in God nullifies previous righteous deeds. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: O you who have believed, obey God and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds… the verse. Whoever among you is able to prevent a good deed from being invalidated by a bad deed, then let him do so. There is no power except with God, for good abrogates evil, and evil abrogates good, and the essence of deeds is their endings.
47:34: And His statement, Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of God and then died while they were disbelievers, God Almighty says: Indeed, those who denied the Oneness of God and averted from that whoever wanted to believe in God and His Messenger, and tempted them away from that, and stood between them and what they wanted of that, then died while they were disbelievers: He says: Then they died while they were in that state of their disbelief, God will not forgive them, He says: God will not pardon what he did of that, but He will punish him for it and disgrace him for it in front of all witnesses.
47:35: God Almighty says: O believers in God, do not be weak in your jihad against the polytheists and do not be cowardly in fighting them. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hussein told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So do not weaken. He said: Do not become weak. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, So do not weaken, do not become weak. His statement, “And you call for peace, while you are the superior ones,” means: Do not be weak against them and call them to peace and reconciliation, while you are the ones who have power over them and are superior to them. And God is with you, means: God will grant you victory over them. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said about this, except that they differed regarding the meaning of His statement, And you are the highest. Some of them said: It means: And you are closer to God than they are. And some of them said something similar to what we have said about it. He mentioned who said that, and he said that the meaning of his saying, And you are the highest, is that you are more deserving of God than they are. Ahmad bin Al-Muqaddam told me: Al-Mu'tamir told us: I heard my father narrating, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, “So do not weaken and call for peace,” he said: That is, do not be the first of the two groups to be defeated. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: “So do not weaken and call for peace.” He said: Do not be the first of the two groups to rush to the other and call for truce, while you are more deserving of God than they are, and God is with you. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muhammar, on the authority of Qatada: “So do not weaken and call for peace.” He said: Do not be the first of the two groups to fall to the other. And you are the superior. He said: He says: And you are more deserving of God than they are. The one who said that mentioned the meaning of his saying, And you are the highest, that you are the victorious ones who are more powerful than them. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And you are the highest, he said: The victorious ones are like the day of Uhud, the circle will be upon them. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about the verse, “So do not weaken and call for peace while you are superior,” that this has been abrogated. He said, “It was abrogated by fighting and jihad. He said, ‘Do not be weak and call them to peace while you are superior.’” He said, “This was when there were treaties and truces between him and the polytheists, before the fighting began. He said, ‘Do not weaken and become weak, so that he thinks that you are calling him to peace while you are above him and more powerful than him. “And you are superior” means you are more powerful than them.’ Then fighting came after this and abrogated all of this. He commanded him to fight them and be harsh with them. It has been said that what he meant by his saying, And you are superior is that you are the victors in the end, even if they defeat you at times and subjugate you in some wars.” His saying, Do not weaken is a jussive mood with a prohibition. As for his saying, and call for there are two aspects: One of them is the jussive mood in conjunction with be weak, so the meaning of the statement is: Do not weaken and do not call for peace. The other is the accusative mood with a declension. His statement, And He will not deprive you of your deeds, means: He will not wrong you in the wages of your deeds, detracting from their reward, from their saying: I killed a man if you killed someone for him and took his money by force. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And He will not deprive you of your deeds, meaning: He will not wrong you in the rewards of your deeds. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And He will not deprive you of your deeds, he said: He will not diminish you. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And He will not deprive you of your deeds means He will not wrong you because of your deeds. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, similarly. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And He will not deprive you of your deeds, that is, He will not wrong you with your deeds. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And He will not deprive you of your deeds, that He said: Your deeds will not wrong you.
47:36: God Almighty says, urging His believing servants to fight His enemies, to spend in His cause, and to sacrifice their lives in fighting the unbelievers: Fight, O believers, the enemies of God and your enemies among the unbelievers, and do not let the desire for life make you abandon fighting them, for the life of this world is only play and amusement, except for that which is for God, of work in His cause and seeking His pleasure. As for what is beyond that, it is only play and amusement, which vanishes and disappears, or a sin that remains for its doer, its shame and disgrace. And if you believe and fear God, He will give you your rewards. He says: And if you work in this world, which has nothing to do with it, it is play and amusement, so you believe in it and fear Him by performing its obligations and avoiding its sins, and it is what remains for you from it, it is not nullified by prolonged play and amusement. Then your Lord will give you your rewards for it, and He will compensate you from it with what is better for you than it on the day of your poverty and your need for your deeds. And He will not ask you for your wealth. He says: And your Lord will not ask you for your wealth, but He commands you to make Him One, and to cast off all rivals besides Him, and to single out divinity and obedience to Him. If they ask you for it, He says: The Most High is Praise: If your Lord asks you for your wealth, He will be stingy with you, He says: He will exhaust you with the request, and will insist on you demanding it from you, so He will swear, Be miserly with it, He says: Be miserly with it and withhold it from Him out of jealousy for it, but He knows This is from you and from your own narrowness, so they did not ask you about it. And His statement, And He will bring forth your grudges, means: And if He, the Most High, were to ask you for your money, He would bring forth your grudges by asking you for that. He said: God knows that by asking you for money, grudges will come forth. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And if you are stingy, then be stingy. He said: Ihfa’ means that you take everything with your hand.
47:37: God Almighty said: If they ask you for it and you are stingy, you will be miserly and they will bring out your grudges.
47:38: God the Most High says to the believers, Here you are O people, these are you who are called to spend in the cause of God meaning: You are called to spend in the struggle against God and in support of His religion. But among you is he who is stingy in spending in it. And the preposition ha was inserted in two places because when the Arabs wanted to make something close, they put the possessive between ha and dha, so they said: Here you are standing, because making something close is an answer to a sentence. So they might repeat ha with dha, or they might suffice with the first, and the second has been deleted. They do not put you before ha because ha is an answer, so it does not make something close to the word. Some Basra grammarians said: The warning was placed in two places for emphasis. And His statement, And whoever is stingy is only stingy to himself, God Almighty says: And whoever is stingy with spending in the way of God is only stingy because of his own stinginess, because if his soul were generous, it would not be stingy with spending in the way of God, but rather it would be generous with it. And God is the Rich, and you are the poor, God Almighty says: God has no need, O people, of your wealth or your expenses, because He is rich and does not need His creation, and creation is poor towards Him, and you are from His creation, so you are the poor towards Him. And He only urged you to spend in His way so that He might gain for you thereby a great reward from Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, “Here you are, you are called upon to spend in the cause of God. But among you is he who is stingy. And whoever is stingy is only stingy with himself. And God is the Free of need, while you are the poor.” He said: God, the Most High, has no need of you, and you are more in need of Him. And the Most High said: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people meaning: If you turn away, O people, from this religion that Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought to you, and turn back from it, He will replace you with another people meaning: He will destroy you and then bring another people in your place who will believe in him and act according to his laws. Then they will not be the likes of you meaning: Then they will not be miserly with what they have been commanded to spend in the way of God, nor will they waste anything of the limits of their religion, but rather they will do all of that as they are commanded. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people. He says: If you turn away from My Book and My obedience, I will replace you with other people. And God, our Lord, is able to do that, to destroy them and bring after them someone better than them. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people. He said: If you turn away from obeying God. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people.... He mentioned that what he meant by his saying, He will replace you with another people is the Persians from the Persians. Who said that? Ibn Buzay` al-Baghdadi Abu Sa`id narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, on the authority of Muslim ibn Khalid, on the authority of al-`Ala` ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “When the verse, ‘And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; Then they will not be the likes of you,' was revealed, Salman was beside the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: 'O Messenger of God, who are these people who, if we turn away, will replace us?' The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, patted Salman on the shoulder and said: 'Who is this man and his people? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if the religion were to hang from the Pleiades, men from Persia would attain it.’” Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Muslim ibn Khalid told me, on the authority of Al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of my father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; Then they will not be the likes of you. They said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who are these people who, if we turn away, will replace us; then they will not be the likes of us? He struck Salman on the thigh and said: This one and his people. Even if the religion were at the Pleiades, men from among the Persians would attain it. Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi narrated: Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Adani narrated: Muslim ibn Khalid narrated on the authority of al-Ala' on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “This verse was revealed while Salman al-Persi was beside the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) scratching his knee: 'And if you turn away, He will replace you with other people; Then they will not be the likes of you.' They said: 'O Messenger of God, who are those who, if we turn away, will be in our place; Then they will not be the likes of us?' He said: Then he struck Salman’s thigh and said: ‘This one and his people.’” Mujahid said about this: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa' told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He will replace you with another people whomever He wills. Others said: They are the people of Yemen. Who said that? Muhammad bin Auf Al-Ta'i told me: Abu Al-Mughirah told us: Sufyan bin Amr told us: Rashid bin Saad, Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubair, and Shureih bin Ubaid told us regarding His statement, And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; Then they will not be the likes of you, he said: The people of Yemen.
